item.title: Breast cancer impacting more young women every year, studies show
item.description: Studies show breast cancer is affecting more young patients every year. Survivors stress the importance of speaking and advocating for yourself. CBS' Jarred Hill has the story of one woman who says she almost didn't get a symptom checked, thinking she was too young.

item.title: From the archives: Paul Stankard's dazzling paperweights
item.description: Glass artist Paul Stankard, whose delicately-crafted paperweights were displayed in museums around the world, died on October 6, 2026 at age 83. In this April 26, 2015 "Sunday Morning" report, Martha Teichner visited Stankard at his New Jersey studio, where the self-taught paperweight-maker demonstrated the remarkable process of creating a tiny world of nature out of glass.

item.title: Foldable iPhone Duo hits market amid debate about price, features
item.description: The first-ever foldable iPhone hit stores nationwide Friday. Apple is playing catch-up — Samsung, Google and Motorola have had folding phones for years. So what are the new features of the first-generation iPhone Duo? And is it worth the hefty price tag? CBS' Evyn Moon reports from Apple's flagship store in New York City.

item.title: The controversy surrounding convicted former election official Tina Peters
item.description: President Trump has gone to extraordinary lengths for Tina Peters, a former Colorado election official convicted for helping to breach the very voting system she swore to protect. Peters served less than two years in prison for crimes related to breaching voting system security. She maintains she was trying to show flaws in the system. 60 Minutes reports, Sunday.

item.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX throttled Ukraine Starlink speeds over drone strikes
item.description: SpaceX's military-grade version of the Starlink internet service has become the backbone of Ukraine's drone operations.

item.title: President Trump, first lady vote early in person in Florida
item.description: President Trump and the first lady voted in Florida before he jetted off to Georgia for a campaign rally.

item.title: DOJ sues to block Alaska Senate certification if Sullivan loses
item.description: The Trump administration is suing to prevent the Alaska Senate election from being certified if GOP Sen. Daniel Sullivan loses to Democrat Mary Peltola because of the other Dan Sullivan who is on the ballot.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Oct. 25)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: More than 1,000 arrested in France as protestors and police clash
item.description: While demonstrations throughout France were largely peaceful, police reported clashes with protesters Saturday evening.

item.title: Malik Beasley negotiating plea deal over NBA betting charges
item.description: The former NBA player has pleaded not guilty to charges that he altered his play in certain games in 2024 to enrich sports bettors and ease his own debts.

item.title: Trump, Vance defend controversial Ramaswamy attack ad; Obama campaigns with Amy Acton
item.description: An ad released by Ohio's Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy has drawn bipartisan backlash. Olivia Gazis has more.

item.title: Deadly shooting in Paris suburb investigated as terrorism, officials say
item.description: A gunman opened fire from his car in the Paris suburb of Trappes on Friday, in what authorities described as a racially motivated act of terrorism.

item.title: Iran says U.S. military not allowed in Gulf "under any circumstance"
item.description: The U.S. ambassador to the U.N. says the war with Iran could last another year, but he hopes Tehran will "come to the table" sooner.

item.title: German man arrested for allegedly driving U.S. teen to die by suicide
item.description: The 18-year-old German was arrested in Hamburg on Thursday, accused of being the indirect perpetrator of murder and grievous bodily harm, prosecutors say.

item.title: Emotional moments as hero dad describes fear and action in face of school shooting
item.description: Oregon dad Kaylub Giamanco was near Silver Rail Elementary School when he had the terrifying realization that a school shooting was underway. He intervened, shooting and killing the teen shooter. Giamanco spoke out about the tragic experience and his heroic actions that saved lives.

item.title: U.K. police confirm it received letter with claims against Meghan's father
item.description: On Friday, it was reported that Meghan's father, Thomas Markle, is under investigation by authorities in the Philippines for alleged possession of child sexual abuse materials.

item.title: 2000s comedy movies marked a golden age, Hollywood critic argues
item.description: Film critic Matt Singer believes the early 2000s were a golden age for comedy movies. His new book "Funny Business" details the rise of the "Frat Pack" genre.

item.title: Rubio calls on Cubans seeking "positive change" to work with CIA
item.description: The CIA posted a video on X showing the steps needed to contact the intelligence agency.

item.title: Chef Ayesha Nurdjaja shares passion for mouthwatering family-style Mediterranean dishes
item.description: Brooklynite chef Ayesha Nurdjaja is executive chef and partner at New York City Mediterranean restaurants Shuka and Shukette. Now she's sharing her favorite zesty recipes in her new cookbook, "Mediterranean All the Way."

item.title: Gray Malin captures natural beauty with jaw-dropping photography
item.description: Author and fine art photographer Gray Malin is renowned for his vibrant conceptual photos and sweeping aerial shots. Malin compiles 15 years of breathtaking wintry photographs taken in places like Aspen and Antarctica in his latest book, "Snow."

item.title: Key politics at play in the 2026 midterms
item.description: Ed O'Keefe has the latest on what you should know ahead of Election Day.

item.title: France braces for another weekend of protests
item.description: France expects another wave of protests over the weekend. Leigh Kiniry reports.

item.title: Eye Opener: Typhoon sweeps through East Asia
item.description: Typhoon Champi brings wind and rain to parts of East Asia, and the search for a new James Bond. All that and all that matters in today's Eye Opener.

item.description: France braces for more protests, plus photographer Gray Malin shares stunning images. All this and more.

item.title: NASA outlines revised 2028 Artemis moon landing campaign
item.description: NASA will not make a decision on whether to use a SpaceX or Blue Origin moon lander until testing shows which one is the obvious choice.

item.title: UFO files detail strange, silent triangular craft: "Acoustic silence"
item.description: Federal agents encountered a large aircraft that zoomed across the sky from a standstill while making no noise or giving off any exhaust, according to new files.

item.title: ICE crackdown prompts some Texas Latinos to turn away from Trump
item.description: "I regret my vote for Biden. Now I regret my vote for Trump," one man said. "What other options do we got?"
